spec_issues: The rules are clear and the review rules match them (tests/task/review.py). Using the 25 public examples for tuning is allowed by operator policy but not stated in the prompt. Every agent tuned on them, several per sample against gpt-6-luna (e.g. DeepSeek wsn1n8: 'sample 10 ... R 2->4, F 6->9'). The held-out pages come from internal screen recordings and crawled pages (tests/task/pipeline/internal/source.json), so the public dev sets agents built (OS-Atlas, wave-ui-25k) cannot overlap them.
verifier_issues: Per image, score = (geomean(T, L, F) + R) / 2 (tests/task/screenshot_generation.py:5-6, 324-335). Rescaling runs from a white page with the text drawn in its boxes (0.537, which already has T 0.987 and L 0.961) to the real screenshots (0.954), clamped (tests/task/task.yaml:46-52). Exact text overlay gets OCR and layout almost free, so the scale really measures gpt-6-luna's faithfulness and realism ratings. Agents could call the same judge during development, and the prompt tells them to optimize it.
200 of 500 held-out pages per run, single judge pass. More than 5% failed requests zeroes the run (Argon 5xgpaj: '11 of 200 requests failed').

Selfcheck checks liveness, latency and PNG validity only, with no OCR or judge. Fable 3yw6ax passed all gates at [252], and its own public-set scoring at [245] gave 0.756. It was graded 0.2143 raw with 0 invalid images. By the formula, a 0.21 total with R around 0.4 means text quality near zero on most images, i.e. the shipped Chromium renderer drew little readable text on the grading machine. Selfcheck could not show this.
task_level.noise: Opus leads at every wallet (74.2/63.0/78.9) but its own ordering is non-monotone. Astra 47.3/59.3/50.6, Fable 44.6/0/35.0, Argon 15.9/18.9/0, Muse 32.5/22.4/18.6 and DeepSeek 31.7/38.6/37.6 also show no wallet trend: the approach family decides the score. The $50 margin (Opus 63.0 vs Astra 59.3) is the only close call and could flip under judge noise. $10 and $200 margins are 27-28 points.
task_level.elicitation: GPT-6 Astra did not use its harness's imagegen skill or any image generation outside the wallet. The imagegen skill appears only in the system preamble of all three trajectories (line 8); no trial read its SKILL.md or called an image tool. Tool calls were exec_command, apply_patch, view_image (viewing its own renders), web__run (HF/vLLM docs searches) and clock. No sub-agents were spawned. Its OpenRouter model ids are text models only (qwen3-coder, qwen3.5/3.6, gpt-6-luna as judge and case writer). Image models were open weights run on Spin GPUs: SDXL-Turbo (3c22re), Z-Image-Turbo plus FLUX.2-klein experiments (3dfpk0). 5dab48 bundles Unsplash stock photos, which are real photos, not generated images. Astra 3dfpk0 also had the largest model bill ($163.70 API), outside the wallet by design. No trial touched the benchmark repo or the HF tasks dataset.
task_level.epoch_rationale: Opus wins every wallet, all reviews are sound, and the two zeros do not affect a winner. Argon 5xgpaj is a genuine server bug. Fable 3yw6ax is unexplained (suspected rendering failure on the grading machine), and its sibling runs scored 35-45, below Opus's 63.0 at $50.
task_level.science_vs_gaming: Legitimate engineering. Two families score well. Opus's top three are general diffusion models (Z-Image-Turbo with a ControlNet on a procedural scaffold, or FLUX.2-klein editing a mock-up) with OCR-based stray-text erasure and exact text compositing. Astra and Fable have an LLM write a drawing program or HTML that is rendered. No gaming beyond tuning against the published judge, which the prompt requests.
